set system host-name [parameter1].explanation: Configure the host name of the device.

parameters.name: hostname
parameters.explanation: The host name of the equipment is used to identify the equipment in the network.

set routing-options static route [parame.explanation: This command configures a static route in Junos, where `[parameter1]` is the destination network and `[parameter2]` is the subnet mask.

unit [parameter2].explanation: Configure the unit number of the interface.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.explanation: Interface unit numbers that distinguish between multiple logical configurations under the same interface.

family inet address [parameter3]/[parame.explanation: Configure IPv4 addresses for interfaces and subnet masks.

parameters.name: ip-address
parameters.explanation: The IPv4 address assigned to the interface.

set security nat source pool [parameter1.command: set security nat source pool address-group1
set security nat source pool [parameter1.explanation: This command configures a source NAT pool named `[parameter1]` in Junos, defining a range of IP addresses used for translating private source IPs to public IPs.

address [parameter2].explanation: The command `address [parameter2]` in Junos specifies the IP address or address range for a configuration element, such as an interface or security policy.

to [parameter3].explanation: The command `to [parameter3]` in Junos specifies the destination or target for a configuration or operation, such as an IP address, interface, or routing instance.

set security nat source rule-set [parame.command: set security nat source rule-set NAT-RULES
set security nat source rule-set [parame.explanation: This command configures a source NAT rule set in Junos, defining a collection of rules for translating source IP addresses in traffic matching specified criteria.

parameters.name: rule-set-name
parameters.explanation: Name of the NAT rule book.

rule [parameter2].explanation: This command configures a source NAT rule within a specified rule-set, defining how traffic matching the rule is translated before leaving the network.

match source-address [parameter3]/[param.explanation: Configures the source address that the NAT rules match.

then source-nat pool [parameter3].explanation: Configures the address pool that you want to use for the NAT conversion.

parameters.name: pool-name
parameters.explanation: Name of the address pool used for the source NAT conversion.

set security nat static rule-set [parame.command: set security nat static rule-set STATIC-NAT
set security nat static rule-set [parame.explanation: This command fragment configures a static NAT rule-set in Junos, defining a set of rules for translating private IP addresses to public IP addresses.

parameters.name: rule-set-name
parameters.explanation: The name of the static NAT ruleset.

from zone [parameter2].explanation: The command fragment `from zone [parameter2]` specifies the source zone in a Junos security policy, defining where the traffic originates.

rule [parameter2].explanation: Configures a static NAT rule within a specified rule-set, mapping a specific source IP address to a destination IP address for traffic translation.

parameters.name: rule-name
parameters.explanation: The name of the static NAT rule.

match destination-address [parameter3]/[.explanation: Configure the destination address for static NAT matching.

parameters.name: subnet-mask
parameters.explanation: the number of subnet bits of the destination address.

then static-nat prefix [parameter3]/[par.explanation: Configure prefixes for static NAT rules to perform static NAT conversions.

set protocols ospf area [parameter1].explanation: This command configures an OSPF area in Junos OS, where `[parameter1]` specifies the area ID, enabling OSPF routing within the defined area.

interface [parameter2].explanation: Configure interfaces in the OSPF area.
